title: Signed ordinary bidual chain map and its localization through the two augmentation comparisons
statement:
Let $(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$ be a ringed site small in the chosen module universe [def-weil-size-convention], with $\mathcal O$ a sheaf of commutative rings. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], their unbounded derived localization $Q$ with category $D(\mathcal O)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], the Hom complex $\mathcal Hom^\bullet$ [def-pur-hom-complex], total tensor [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], K-flat complexes [def-pc-kflat-complex], and $H=R\mathcal Hom$ with its fixed K-injective augmentations $\eta_F:F\to I(F)$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Fix the closed symmetric monoidal structure and its canonical K-flat tensor and uncurrying models [def-coef-ringed-tensor-hom-model, lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal]. Write $\operatorname{tr}$ for its right-tensor adjunction and $\epsilon_{L,M}:H(L,M)\otimes^{\mathbf L}L\to M$ for its counit. Write $O=\mathcal O[0]$ and also $O$ for its derived image. For an arbitrary complex $E$ put $D=\mathcal Hom^\bullet(E,O)$. There is a unique chain map
$$\beta_E:E\to\mathcal Hom^\bullet(D,O)$$
whose evaluation on local homogeneous sections is
$$\beta_E(x)(\phi)=(-1)^{a q}\phi(x)\quad(x\in E^a,\ \phi\in D^q,\ a+q=0),$$
with every Hom-product component landing in a nonzero degree of $O$ equal to zero. Thus this is a statement about the actual product-defined Hom complex, not only about its derived image. The maps $\beta_E$ are natural in chain maps $E\to E'$. Let
$$b_A=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(A\otimes^{\mathbf L}H(A,O)\xrightarrow{\sigma}H(A,O)\otimes^{\mathbf L}A\xrightarrow{\epsilon_{A,O}}O\bigr),$$
where $\sigma$ is the Koszul symmetry. Suppose $\mathcal Hom^\bullet(E,\eta_O)$ and $\mathcal Hom^\bullet(D,\eta_O)$ are quasi-isomorphisms. They induce canonical isomorphisms $\gamma_E:QD\xrightarrow{\sim}H(QE,O)$ and $\gamma_D:Q\mathcal Hom^\bullet(D,O)\xrightarrow{\sim}H(QD,O)$. Then
$$H(\gamma_E,O)\circ b_{QE}=\gamma_D\circ Q(\beta_E).$$
This equation uses the canonical normalized tensor-Hom models, and requires no K-flatness of $E$ or $D$, no boundedness, and no perfectness.

proof.text: Construct the signed evaluation for any target complex O, before specializing to the coefficient unit. In degree a use the product limit defining Hom(Hom(E,O),O)^a. Its q projection is (-1)^(a*q) times the transpose of localized evaluation E^a -> Hom(Hom(E^a,O^(q+a)),O^(q+a)), precomposed in the inner Hom with the actual product projection. The already proved presheaf tensor curry and uncurry constructions supply this localized evaluation. Its formula on every slice object is (-1)^(a*q) phi(x restricted). After specializing O to the degree-zero coefficient unit, all components with q+a nonzero are zero. Product and localized sheaf-Hom extensionality imply uniqueness.

proof.text: Check the chain-map equation on every product projection and every localized section, still for arbitrary O. Expand the outer and inner Hom differentials. Naturality of the differential of E moves it through restriction. The two terms involving d_O cancel, while the remaining sign is (-1)^((a+1)*q), since (-1)^(a+a*(q+1)+q)=(-1)^((a+1)*q). This proves the equation in all degrees, including negative degrees; no boundedness or sum over product components is used.

source.place: Tag 0A8X (section-hom-complexes), displayed differential; explicit coefficient-unit sign calculation for Tag 0A92 (lemma-evaluate-and-more).

proof.text:
For a chain map $f:E\to E'$ write $D(f)=\mathcal Hom^\bullet(f,O):D'\to D$. For $x\in E^a$ and $\phi\in(D')^q$ the two composites have the same component
$$ \beta_{E'}(f(x))(\phi)=(-1)^{a q}\phi(f(x))=\beta_E(x)(D(f)(\phi)). $$
All other components are zero. Equality on each restriction and each Hom-product projection proves $\beta_{E'}f=\mathcal Hom^\bullet(D(f),O)\beta_E$, the asserted naturality.

proof.text: Define comparison(E,O) as Q(Hom(E,eta_O)) followed by the inverse fixed coefficientHomResolutionIso. Naturality in E is precisely naturality of the inverse Localization.fac isomorphism, together with naturality of Hom in the two variables. The subsequent derived comparison is proved as an equation of morphisms before any augmentation hypothesis. Under the two hypotheses in the statement, Q(Hom(E,eta_O)) and Q(Hom(D,eta_O)) are isomorphisms, and composing their asIso with the fixed factorization inverse supplies gamma_E and gamma_D with the specified homs.

proof.text: Choose K-flat flat-term resolutions p:P -> E and t:T -> D. Put I=I(O), g=t followed by Hom(p,O) and Hom(P,eta_O), and h=p followed by beta_E, Hom(t,O), and Hom(T,eta_O). Naturality of the fixed localization factorization identifies Qg followed by its inverse factorization with Qt followed by comparison(E,O) and H(Qp,O). Likewise Qh followed by its inverse factorization is Qp followed by Qbeta_E, comparison(D,O), and H(Qt,O). Only Qp and Qt need to be invertible here; no separate Hom quasi-isomorphism-invariance theorem is used.

source.place: Tag 06YS (lemma-K-flat-resolution); Tag 0A95 (lemma-RHom-well-defined); Tag 08J7 (section-internal-hom), fixed representative functoriality.

proof.text:
Apply the stipulated normalized tensor-Hom model to $g$ and the K-flat pair $T,P$. With the canonical tensor comparison, its derived uncurrying is $(Q\eta)^{-1}Q(u)$, where
$$ u:\operatorname{Tot}(T\otimes P)\to J,\qquad u(\tau\otimes x)=\eta\bigl(t(\tau)(p(x))\bigr). $$
A component with $|\tau|+|x|\ne0$ is zero, since $g$ factors through Hom into $O$. This identifies the map without a choice of evaluation: by the counit formula for transposition and $Qg=H(Qp,O)\gamma_EQt$, its uncurrying is also
$$ \epsilon_{QE,O}\circ(\gamma_EQt\otimes^{\mathbf L}Qp):QT\otimes^{\mathbf L}QP\to O. $$
The latter equality is exactly naturality of the adjunction in its right tensor argument $P\to E$. The two K-flat inputs are $T,P$, so every hypothesis of the given representative normalization is satisfied.

source.place: Tag 08J9 (lemma-internal-hom), normalized uncurrying and naturality of equation-internal-hom; coefficient-unit evaluation in Tag 0A97 (lemma-internal-hom-evaluate).

proof.text:
Apply the same normalization to $h$ and the K-flat pair $P,T$. Its uncurrying is $(Q\eta)^{-1}Q(v)$, where
$$ v:\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes T)\to J,\qquad v(x\otimes\tau)=\eta\bigl(\beta_E(p(x))(t(\tau))\bigr)=(-1)^{a q}\eta\bigl(t(\tau)(p(x))\bigr) $$
for $x\in P^a$, $\tau\in T^q$ with $a+q=0$, and is zero otherwise. The actual total-complex symmetry $s_{P,T}$ has formula $x\otimes\tau\mapsto(-1)^{a q}\tau\otimes x$. Consequently $v=u\circ s_{P,T}$ on every pure generator in every coproduct summand. These are equal chain maps: the sheaf tensor is the sheafification of the sectionwise tensor, so the bilinear formulas determine each summand map, and the coproduct inclusions determine the total map. The specified derived symmetry is induced by this same symmetry on K-flat representatives; hence uncurrying $Qh$ gives the uncurrying of $Qg$ composed with $\sigma_{QP,QT}$.

source.place: Tags 0A8X and 0A92 (section-hom-complexes; lemma-evaluate-and-more), explicit signs; Tag 0FPT (lemma-symmetric-monoidal-derived), symmetry on K-flat representatives; sites-modules Tag 03EK (section-tensor-product), sheafification tensor.

proof.text:
For the other side of the desired equality, naturality of transposition, the definition of $b_{QE}$ and naturality of symmetry show that the uncurrying of
$$ H(Qt,O)H(\gamma_E,O)b_{QE}Qp $$
is
$$ \epsilon_{QE,O}\circ(\gamma_EQt\otimes^{\mathbf L}Qp)\circ\sigma_{QP,QT}. $$
Indeed, first precomposing the first Hom argument by $\gamma_EQt$ tensors the evaluation with this map; then $\sigma_{QE,H(QE,O)}\circ(Qp\otimes^{\mathbf L}\gamma_EQt)=(\gamma_EQt\otimes^{\mathbf L}Qp)\circ\sigma_{QP,QT}$. Steps 6 and 7 identify this with the uncurrying of $Qh=H(Qt,O)\gamma_DQ(\beta_E)Qp$. The adjunction bijection therefore identifies these maps $QP\to H(QT,O)$. Cancel the isomorphisms $Qp$ and $H(Qt,O)$ to obtain
$$ H(\gamma_E,O)b_{QE}=\gamma_DQ(\beta_E). $$
All comparisons used only resolutions of $E,D$, their two assumed augmentation quasi-isomorphisms, and the stipulated normalized models; no boundedness or perfectness enters.
